correctness.rationale: For the coefficients \(a_k=\exp(k/\log\log k)\) with \(k\ge2000\), direct differentiation gives a strictly concave positive exponent with \(g\prime\to0\). Every \(r\) sufficiently near \(1\) has a unique continuous saddle \(x\), with height \(H=x/(uL^2)\) where \(u=\log x\) and \(L=\log u\). The Taylor block of width \(\lfloor\sqrt{xu}L/10\rfloor\) has at least \(\sqrt{xu}L/10\) terms of size \(\exp(H-1/100)\), while \(\mu\le e^H\). Combining \(1-r\ge1/(4L)\), \(\log A\le2H\), and \(\log_2 A\le u\) proves a lower quotient \(L/(40e\sqrt2)\to\infty\) and \(\log_3 A\sim L\). The coefficient root test gives radius exactly \(1\); positivity gives \(M=f(r)\). Symbolic checks and finite diagnostics support, but do not replace, the infinite analytic proof.
